subject: Request: annotated subprocessor matrix + egress jurisdiction map
messages:
From: Jin Park <jin.park@acmepayments.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-security@acmepayments.com
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor inventory + egress jurisdictions (needed for onboarding)

Hi Lauren,

Hope you're well — we're finalizing the onboarding packet for Acme's payments integration and need a couple of items from Redwood for our security review. Specifically: 

1) An "annotated subprocessor roster" that lists each third-party processor (name, role, data types processed, country of processing, and whether they have access to raw transaction data).
2) A simple egress/jurisdiction map that shows where customer data may transit or be stored (EU/US/APAC) and any onshore-only processors.

I've attached a short PDF that shows the format our security team prefers (acme_subprocessor_request.pdf). We aim to close the security review by next Friday (10/7). Can you confirm if Redwood can provide these items and estimate a delivery date? Also let us know if you can provide attestations (SOC2 snapshot, KMS region, or contract clause references) alongside the roster.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Jin Park
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments
Attachment: acme_subprocessor_request.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jin Park <jin.park@acmepayments.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor inventory + egress jurisdictions (needed for onboarding)

Hi Jin — thanks for the clear template and timeline. We can provide an annotated roster and an egress/jurisdiction summary.

Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Rishi (Privacy/Infrastructure) to manage the details and any contract references. Preliminary estimate: we should be able to deliver a first-pass annotated roster and egress map within 48–72 hours, and a more formal package (with SOC2 snapshot and KMS region statement) within 5 business days.

Kimberly / Rishi — can you take point on preparing the matrix in the attached template? Two questions for the security team to confirm: 1) Do you need per-tenant residency carveouts (i.e., a column for whether a processor is allowed to process EU-only tenants), and 2) Do you require us to include historical retention policies per processor in this deliverable?

I'll mark this as high priority and follow up with Rishi for any infra-level exports.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Technical Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 13:20:45 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Subprocessor inventory + egress jurisdictions (draft roster attached)

Hi all — drafting the annotated roster now and attaching an initial workbook (annotated_roster_v1.xlsx). Notes/assumptions included on the first sheet.

Key callouts:
- One telemetry vendor (EdgeSight Analytics) is strictly onshore for EU customers (processing in DE). We flagged that in the "onshore_only" column.
- Our CDN provider has regional POPs but does not persist raw transaction data; we marked as "transit" for data type scope.
- For processors that are simply pass-through (e.g., cloud egress proxies), we've added a "transit_only" note instead of raw-data access.

Questions for Acme security to confirm before we finalize:
1) Do you require an explicit exportability statement per-processor (yes/no)?
2) For PCI-scope processors, do you need evidence files (e.g., PCI attestation) attached to this packet, or is a reference to our compliance catalogue sufficient?

I linked the working draft in our shared drive: https://drive.company/shared/annotated_roster_drafts/lauren_kimberly_v1 (internal).

Attachment: annotated_roster_v1.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 42KB)

Cc: ops-security@acmepayments.com
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor inventory + egress jurisdictions (needed for onboarding)

Thanks Kimberly and Lauren — this looks great and the draft roster is exactly what we had in mind. A few quick replies to your questions: 

1) Exportability statement: yes please — a simple Y/N column per processor is helpful.
2) PCI evidence: a reference to Redwood's compliance catalogue is fine for initial review; we may ask for copies during procurement but please include links or IDs in the workbook.

Also: for the onshore-only flag, can you ensure the cell includes the controlling legal entity (e.g., "EdgeSight Analytics EU Ops GmbH (DE)") so our legal team can cross-check registrations?

One small ask — can you also export a CSV version of the final roster (machine-readable) so we can ingest into our tracker? If you can provide the CSV and a final signed attestation by 10/7, procurement can proceed on our side.

Happy to set a quick 20-minute sync if that accelerates things.

Best,
Jin
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments
